dna.label: PP-00005
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Two sets of concentric rings offset from each other — interference creates moire.

body.expr: eps = 0.005; px = x * scale + t * drift; py = y * scale; nr = noise2(px + eps, py); nl = noise2(px - eps, py); nu = noise2(px, py + eps); nd = noise2(px, py - eps); vx = nu - nd; vy = -(nr - nl); angle = atan2(vy, vx); 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(angle * bands + t * speed)

dna.label: PP-00004
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Curl noise: treats scalar noise as a stream function, visualizes flow direction via atan2. From computational fluid dynamics.

dna.label: PP-00003
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Chladni plate vibration patterns. Sand gathers at the nodal lines where z = 0. Mode numbers control the star count.

dna.label: PP-00002
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Classic plasma: sum of sines at different scales and angles. Demoscene lineage.

body.expr: px = x * scale; py = y * scale; qx = noise2(px + t * speed, py); qy = noise2(px + 5.2, py + 1.3); rx = noise2(px + warp * qx + 1.7, py + warp * qy + 9.2); ry = noise2(px + warp * qx + 8.3, py + warp * qy + 2.8); 0.5 + 0.5 * noise2(px + warp * rx, py + warp * ry)

dna.label: PP-00001
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Domain warping — warp 1 is the glass, warp 2 is the body under the glass. Liquid, marble, smoke.

body.expr: px = abs(x - 0.5); py = y - 0.5; sx = sin(angle * 0.5); cy = cos(angle * 0.5); ex = px - sx * radius; ey = py - cy * radius; d1 = sqrt(ex * ex + ey * ey); d2 = abs(sqrt(px * px + py * py) - radius); d = (cy * px > sx * py ? d1 : d2) - thick; smoothstep(blur, 0.0, d)

dna.label: PP-00007
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Inigo Quilez 2D SDF — arc (ring segment). A curved stroke: radius sets the sweep, angle sets the angular extent, thick inflates the centreline into a band. Outside the angular range, distance falls to the nearest endpoint cap. Pie fills a sector; Arc traces its rim. Source: iquilezles.org/articles/distfunctions2d

body.expr: sx = x * scale; sy = y * scale; cx = floor(sx); cy = floor(sy); fx = sx - cx; fy = sy - cy; parity = (cx + cy) - floor((cx + cy) * 0.5) * 2.0; bx = smoothstep(0.0, gap, fx) * smoothstep(0.0, gap, 1.0 - fx); by = smoothstep(0.0, gap, fy) * smoothstep(0.0, gap, 1.0 - fy); inner = parity > 0.5 ? smoothstep(0.0, gap, abs(fy - 0.5)) : smoothstep(0.0, gap, abs(fx - 0.5)); bx * by * inner

dna.label: PP-00008
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Basketweave tile pattern — alternating cells split horizontally or vertically based on checkerboard parity. Cell boundaries give the outer mortar, inner split gives the brick subdivisions. The parquet floor and woven textile share this bone structure. Distinct from BrickTile (offset rows) and WovenGrid (sinusoidal). Source: Book of Shaders pattern chapter, adapted to tile-parity logic.

body.expr: qx = floor(x * samples) / samples; wave = sin(qx * carrier + y * ymod) * cos(qx * detune + t * speed); 0.5 + 0.5 * wave

dna.label: PP-00009
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Deliberately undersampled sine from t06_245 beat-frequency taste. Two frequencies (carrier and detune) sampled at a third rate. The aliasing IS the pattern — Nyquist violations as design material. The beat frequency emerges where carrier and detune drift apart.

body.expr: gx = floor(x * cols); gy = floor(y * rows); fx = x * cols - gx; fy = y * rows - gy; gate = sin(gx * wfreq - gy + t * speed) > 0.0 ? 1.0 : 0.0; face = 0.5 + (fx < bw ? 0.3 : 0.0) + (fy < bw ? 0.3 : 0.0) - (fx > 1.0 - bw ? 0.3 : 0.0) - (fy > 1.0 - bw ? 0.3 : 0.0); face * gate

dna.label: PP-0000A
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Beveled tiles with plane-wave gate from t06_236. Three-rect bevel per cell — highlight on left/top edges, shadow on right/bottom, flat face between. The wave gate selects which tiles are lit. 'Shiny Maya stuff with no light in the code' — the bevel IS the light.

body.expr: p0x = -bspan; p0y = -bcurve; p1x = 0.0; p1y = bcurve; p2x = bspan; p2y = -bcurve; ppx = x - 0.5; ppy = y - 0.5; aax = p1x - p0x; aay = p1y - p0y; bbx = p0x - 2.0 * p1x + p2x; bby = p0y - 2.0 * p1y + p2y; ccx = aax * 2.0; ccy = aay * 2.0; ddx = p0x - ppx; ddy = p0y - ppy; kk = 1.0 / (bbx * bbx + bby * bby + 0.000000001); kx = kk * (aax * bbx + aay * bby); ky = kk * (2.0 * (aax * aax + aay * aay) + ddx * bbx + ddy * bby) / 3.0; kz = kk * (ddx * aax + ddy * aay); ppp = ky - kx * kx; p3 = ppp * ppp * ppp; qqq = kx * (2.0 * kx * kx - 3.0 * ky) + kz; hhh = qqq * qqq + 4.0 * p3; sh = sqrt(max(abs(hhh), 0.0)); ux_raw = (sh - qqq) / 2.0; vx_raw = (-sh - qqq) / 2.0; ux_sgn = ux_raw > 0.0 ? 1.0 : -1.0; vx_sgn = vx_raw > 0.0 ? 1.0 : -1.0; ux = ux_sgn * pow(max(abs(ux_raw), 0.000000001), 0.333333333); vx = vx_sgn * pow(max(abs(vx_raw), 0.000000001), 0.333333333); t1 = clamp(ux + vx - kx, 0.0, 1.0); e1x = ddx + (ccx + bbx * t1) * t1; e1y = ddy + (ccy + bby * t1) * t1; res1 = e1x * e1x + e1y * e1y; zz = sqrt(max(-ppp, 0.000000001)); vvv = acos(clamp(qqq / (ppp * zz * 2.0 + 0.000000001), -1.0, 1.0)) / 3.0; mm = cos(vvv); nn = sin(vvv) * 1.732050808; ta = clamp((mm + mm) * zz - kx, 0.0, 1.0); tb2 = clamp((-nn - mm) * zz - kx, 0.0, 1.0); ea1x = ddx + (ccx + bbx * ta) * ta; ea1y = ddy + (ccy + bby * ta) * ta; ra1 = ea1x * ea1x + ea1y * ea1y; ea2x = ddx + (ccx + bbx * tb2) * tb2; ea2y = ddy + (ccy + bby * tb2) * tb2; ra2 = ea2x * ea2x + ea2y * ea2y; res2 = min(ra1, ra2); res = hhh > 0.0 ? res1 : res2; d = sqrt(max(res, 0.0)) - bthick; smoothstep(blur, 0.0, d)

dna.label: PP-0000B
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Inigo Quilez 2D SDF — quadratic Bezier curve. Three control points define a parabolic arc; the closest point is found by solving a depressed cubic. The bspan parameter sets horizontal spread, bcurve the vertical sag, bthick adds stroke width. Parameterized as a symmetric S-curve for composability. Source: iquilezles.org/articles/distfunctions2d

body.expr: px = abs(x - 0.5); py = abs(y - 0.5); ax = abs(px - py) * 0.70710678; ay = (1.0 - px - py) * 0.70710678; pp = (bhe - ay - 0.25 / bhe) / (6.0 * bhe); qq = ax / (bhe * bhe * 16.0); hh = qq * qq - pp * pp * pp; rr = sqrt(max(hh, 0.0)); cb1 = pow(max(qq + rr, 0.000000001), 0.333333333); qmr = abs(qq - rr); cb2 = pow(max(qmr, 0.000000001), 0.333333333); sgn_qr = rr > qq ? 1.0 : -1.0; x1 = cb1 - cb2 * sgn_qr; r2 = sqrt(max(pp, 0.000000001)); pr = pp * r2; aarg = clamp(qq / (abs(pr) > 0.000000001 ? pr : 0.000000001), -1.0, 1.0); x2 = 2.0 * r2 * cos(acos(aarg) / 3.0); xf = hh > 0.0 ? x1 : x2; xf = min(xf, 0.70710678); zx = xf - ax; zy = bhe * (1.0 - 2.0 * xf * xf) - ay; d = sqrt(zx * zx + zy * zy) * (zy > 0.0 ? 1.0 : -1.0); smoothstep(blur, 0.0, d)

dna.label: PP-0000C
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Inigo Quilez 2D SDF — blobby cross. A soft, organic four-lobed shape. Rotates coordinates 45 degrees, then solves a depressed cubic (Cardano + trig) to find the closest point on the implicit curve y = he*(1-2x^2). The bhe parameter controls blobbiness. Source: iquilezles.org/articles/distfunctions2d

body.expr: dx = x - 0.5; dy = y - 0.5; d = sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy) * scale; abs(sin(d * 3.14159 * bounces)) * pow(2.71828, 0.0 - d * decay)

dna.label: PP-0000D
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Bouncing-ball spatial gradient: abs(sin) gives the bounce oscillation, exp(-d) gives the decay envelope. Together they model a ball bouncing with decreasing height — applied radially from centre. The bounces param controls oscillation frequency, decay controls how quickly the amplitude dies off. Mined from LYGIA animation/easing bounce-out function, applied spatially.

body.expr: qx = abs(x - 0.5) - bx; qy = abs(y - 0.5) - by; mx = max(qx, 0.0); my = max(qy, 0.0); d = sqrt(mx * mx + my * my) + min(max(qx, qy), 0.0); smoothstep(blur, 0.0, d)

dna.label: PP-0000E
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Inigo Quilez 2D SDF — axis-aligned box. The fundamental rectangle SDF: abs for symmetry, max for interior distance, Euclidean for exterior corners. Every UI element starts here. Source: iquilezles.org/articles/distfunctions2d

body.expr: dx = x - 0.5; dy = y - 0.5; d = sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy); a = atan2(dy, dx); r_pulse = base_radius + pulse * sin(t * speed * 6.28318); thick_vary = 0.015 + 0.01 * sin(a * segments + t * speed * 3.0); ring = 1.0 - abs(d - r_pulse) / thick_vary; clamp(ring, 0.0, 1.0)

dna.label: PP-0000F
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Ring that pulses in radius with sine modulation, thickness varies around the perimeter. From t06 ring/pulse patterns.

dna.label: PP-00010
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Offset-row tiling: odd rows shift by half a brick width. Smoothstep mortar lines give soft-edged joints. The ur-pattern of architectural texture — from Book of Shaders pattern chapter. Every brick wall is this equation plus noise.

dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Overlapping refracted light rings simulating underwater caustics. From t06_026 caustic readings.

dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Voronoi cellular noise — the four-channel cell. st_007 in taste_07. F1 is blobs, F2-F1 is borders, cell ID is crystals in a metal. Jitter 0 snaps to hexagons, 1 is organic.

dna.label: PP-00013
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: fract/floor tiling with per-cell random brightness from cellnoise. Cell size is the room, shape size is the tenant. From st_003/st_009 in taste_07.

dna.label: PP-00014
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Inigo Quilez 2D SDF — chamfered box. A rectangle with the corners cut at 45 degrees. Chamfer controls how much of each corner is removed (0 = sharp rectangle, larger = more cut). The frame, the gem, the machined edge. Source: iquilezles.org/articles/distfunctions2d

dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Pipeline proof: simplest per-pixel pattern. From st_009 fract/floor in taste_07.

body.expr: dx = x - 0.5; dy = y - 0.5; d = sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy); fade = pow(2.71828, -d * decay); v = sin(d * d * freq - t * speed) * fade; clamp(0.5 + 0.5 * v, 0.0, 1.0)

dna.label: PP-00016
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Chirp wave from t06_183 jellyfish taste — sin(d^2) makes spatial frequency increase with distance from centre. Tight rings at the rim, broad pulse at the core. The radar sweep, the water drop, the sonar ping.

body.expr: px = x - 0.5; py = y - 0.5; d = sqrt(px * px + py * py) - radius; smoothstep(blur, 0.0, d)

dna.label: PP-00017
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Inigo Quilez 2D SDF — circle. length(p) - r. The simplest possible SDF and the atom of the entire shape library. Every other shape is this one deformed. Source: iquilezles.org/articles/distfunctions2d

body.expr: px = x - 0.5; py = y - 0.5; tb2 = 3.1415927 * 5.0 / 6.0 * max(tb, 0.0001); cox = ra * sin(tb2); coy = ra * cos(tb2); period = cox * 4.0; mx = px - period * floor(px / period); px2 = abs(mx - cox * 2.0); p1x = px2; p1y = py; p2x = abs(px2 - 2.0 * cox); p2y = -py + 2.0 * coy; v1x = p1x - cox; v1y = p1y - coy; l1 = sqrt(v1x * v1x + v1y * v1y); al1 = sqrt(p1x * p1x + p1y * p1y); d1 = coy * p1x > cox * p1y ? l1 : abs(al1 - ra); v2x = p2x - cox; v2y = p2y - coy; l2 = sqrt(v2x * v2x + v2y * v2y); al2 = sqrt(p2x * p2x + p2y * p2y); d2 = coy * p2x > cox * p2y ? l2 : abs(al2 - ra); d = min(d1, d2) - thick; smoothstep(blur, 0.0, d)

dna.label: PP-00018
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Inigo Quilez 2D SDF — circle wave. A horizontally repeating sinusoidal wave made from arc segments. Uses GLSL-style mod (floor-based) for tiling. The tb parameter controls arc openness, ra the radius, thick adds stroke width. Source: iquilezles.org/articles/distfunctions2d

body.expr: gx = floor(x * cells); gy = floor(y * cells); lx = x * cells - gx - 0.5; ly = y * cells - gy - 0.5; tcx = (gx + 0.5) / cells; tcy = (gy + 0.5) / cells; ax = 0.5 + reach * sin(2.0 * t); ay = 0.5 + reach * sin(2.9 * t); angle = atan2(ay - tcy, ax - tcx) + 1.5708; perp = abs(lx * sin(angle) - ly * cos(angle)); along = abs(lx * cos(angle) + ly * sin(angle)); (perp < thick ? 1.0 : 0.0) * (along < len ? 1.0 : 0.0)

dna.label: PP-00019
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Hair-comb vector field from t06_229. Each tile draws a line segment perpendicular to the direction toward a Lissajous attractor. The +PI/2 offset means the needles trace contour lines, not compass bearings. The field combs itself as the attractor drifts.

body.expr: dx = x - 0.5; dy = y - 0.5; d = sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy); 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(d * frequency - t * speed)

dna.label: PP-0001A
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Concentric rings from centre with time animation. st_010 step/smoothstep on distance — the falloff law wearing its equation.

body.expr: n = 0.5 + 0.5 * noise2(x * scale + t * drift, y * scale); 0.5 + 0.5 * cos(n * bands * 6.28318)

dna.label: PP-0001B
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Contour-banding from t06_044 — cos of field equals free topo lines. The net curtains reading. Water contours, topographic maps, terrain.

body.expr: sy = y + t * speed; gx = floor(x * grid_size); gy = floor(sy * grid_size); cx = (gx + 0.5) / grid_size; cy = (gy + 0.5) / grid_size; dy_c = sy - cy; dx_c = x - cx; d = sqrt(dx_c * dx_c + dy_c * dy_c) * grid_size; rx = cx - 0.5; ry = (cy - floor(cy)) - 0.5; rd = sqrt(rx * rx + ry * ry); fall = 1.0 / (1.0 + rd * rd * falloff * falloff); r = 0.35 * fall; smoothstep(r, r * 0.6, d)

dna.label: PP-0001C
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Dots on a vertical conveyor belt with radial size falloff from centre. t06_034 lattice conveyor.

body.expr: px_raw = (x - 0.5) / scale; py_raw = (y - 0.5) / scale; six = py_raw < 0.0 ? -px_raw : px_raw; px = abs(px_raw); qy = abs(py_raw) - 0.2; rex = px - min(round(px / 0.4), 0.4); aby = abs(qy - 0.2) - 0.6; c1 = clamp(0.5 * (six - qy), 0.0, 0.2); v1x = six - c1; v1y = -qy - c1; dd = v1x * v1x + v1y * v1y; c2 = clamp(0.5 * (px - aby), 0.0, 0.4); v2x = px - c2; v2y = -aby - c2; dd = min(dd, v2x * v2x + v2y * v2y); c3 = clamp(qy, 0.0, 0.4); v3x = rex; v3y = qy - c3; dd = min(dd, v3x * v3x + v3y * v3y); s = 2.0 * px + aby + abs(aby + 0.4) - 0.4; d = sqrt(dd) * (s > 0.0 ? 1.0 : -1.0) * scale; smoothstep(blur, 0.0, d)

dna.label: PP-0001D
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Inigo Quilez 2D SDF — the Cool S (Super S / Stussy S). The iconic S-shape doodled on every schoolkid's notebook. Six line segments, no curves — the distance is computed to each segment and minimized. Scale controls overall size. Source: iquilezles.org/articles/distfunctions2d

body.expr: 0.5 + 0.5 * cos(6.28318 * (freq * x + phase + t * speed))

dna.label: PP-0001E
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Inigo Quilez cosine palette formula: a + b*cos(2pi*(c*t+d)). Here as a greyscale wave across x. The basis of all IQ procedural color work, reduced to one channel. Frequency sets the number of oscillations, phase slides the pattern, speed animates.

body.expr: f1 = voronoi2(x * scale + t * drift, y * scale, 1, 1.0); f2 = voronoi2(x * scale + t * drift, y * scale, 2, 1.0); border = f2 - f1; smoothstep(0.0, crack_width, border)

dna.label: PP-0001F
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Voronoi F2-F1 (border distance), creating cracked/cellular boundaries. st_007 voronoi borders.

body.expr: px = x - 0.5; py = abs(y - 0.5); d1 = sqrt(px * px + py * py) - outer; d2 = sqrt((px - offset) * (px - offset) + py * py) - inner; d = max(d1, -d2); smoothstep(blur, 0.0, d)

dna.label: PP-00020
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Crescent moon via SDF boolean subtraction: max(circle, -circle). Outer circle defines the body, inner circle (offset sideways) carves the bite. Three params give full control — from thin sickle to fat gibbous. The oldest shape in the sky, now a distance field. Source: iquilezles.org/articles/distfunctions2d (sdMoon simplified to boolean form).

body.expr: hd = max(abs(x - 0.5) - arm, abs(y - 0.5) - thick); vd = max(abs(x - 0.5) - thick, abs(y - 0.5) - arm); d = min(hd, vd); smoothstep(blur, 0.0, d)

dna.label: PP-00021
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Union of two box SDFs — horizontal arm and vertical arm. Medical cross, crosshair, or plus sign as a signed distance field. Arm controls reach, thick controls bar width, blur softens edges. Source: SDF boolean union min(d1,d2) from IQ's 2D distance functions.

body.expr: ppx = abs(x - 0.5); ppy = abs(y - 0.5); sx = ppy > ppx ? ppy : ppx; sy = ppy > ppx ? ppx : ppy; qx = sx - arm; qy = sy - thick; k = max(qy, qx); wx = k > 0.0 ? qx : thick - sx; wy = k > 0.0 ? qy : -k; mwx = max(wx, 0.0); mwy = max(wy, 0.0); d = (k > 0.0 ? 1.0 : -1.0) * sqrt(mwx * mwx + mwy * mwy) + rnd; smoothstep(blur, 0.0, d)

dna.label: PP-00022
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Inigo Quilez 2D SDF — cross with rounded inner corners. Unlike CrossField (union of two boxes) or RoundedCross (rounded elbows), this uses a single distance function with an explicit rounding parameter. Negative rnd smooths the inner concave corners; positive rnd inflates the entire shape. Source: iquilezles.org/articles/distfunctions2d

body.expr: wave = sin(y * wave_freq * 6.28318 + t * speed) * wave_amount; lx = (x + wave) * lines; frac = lx - floor(lx); d = abs(frac - 0.5); smoothstep(0.1, 0.0, d)

dna.label: PP-00023
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Vertical wavy lines like net curtains or rain. t06_044 net curtains.

body.expr: px = abs(x - 0.5); py = y - 0.5; w = sqrt(max(radius * radius - cut * cut, 0.0)); s = max((cut - radius) * px * px + w * w * (cut + radius - 2.0 * py), cut * px - w * py); dl = sqrt(px * px + py * py) - radius; dc = cut - py; de = sqrt((px - w) * (px - w) + (py - cut) * (py - cut)); d = s < 0.0 ? dl : (px < w ? dc : de); smoothstep(blur, 0.0, d)

dna.label: PP-00024
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Inigo Quilez 2D SDF — circle with a horizontal flat cut. Cut controls where the slice goes: negative keeps more disk, positive keeps less. Three-way distance: body of circle, flat edge, or corner. Useful for D-pads, truncated shapes, and any circle that needs a flat bottom. Source: iquilezles.org/articles/distfunctions2d

dna.label: PP-00025
dna.author: makers-factory

dna.label: PP-00026
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Diagonal line pattern with noise displacement — order meets chaos. From t06 diagonal patterns.

dna.label: PP-00027
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Six-source wave interference: 6 point sources arranged in a regular hexagon emit circular wavefronts (sin of distance). Superposition creates constructive/destructive interference — bright maxima where waves align, dark minima where they cancel. The pattern is the 2D analogue of a hexagonal diffraction grating. Mined from Shadertoy wave interference simulations.

body.expr: gx = floor(x * cells); gy = floor(y * cells); h = abs(sin(gx * 127.1 + gy * 311.7 + t * speed) * 43758.5453); h - floor(h)

dna.label: PP-00028
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Per-cell hash with time injection — from st_019 hash function in taste_07. Each tile gets a pseudo-random brightness that cycles over time. Speed at zero = static stained glass. Speed up = disco floor.

body.expr: gx = floor(x * dots); gy = floor(y * dots); cx = (gx + 0.5) / dots; cy = (gy + 0.5) / dots; dx = (x - cx) * dots; dy = (y - cy) * dots; d = sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy); r = dot_size + 0.05 * sin(t * speed + gx * 0.5 + gy * 0.7); smoothstep(r, r * 0.8, d)

dna.label: PP-00029
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Regular grid of circular dots, useful as a halftone source. Utility/halftone foundation.

body.expr: dx = x - 0.5; dy = y - 0.5; r = sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy) + 0.0001; lnr = log(r); th = atan2(dy, dx); sn = 0.0 - log(max(zoom, 0.01)) / 6.28318; nl = pow(2.71828, lnr - th * sn); na = sn * lnr + th + t * speed; nx = nl * cos(na) * scale; ny = nl * sin(na) * scale; 0.5 + 0.5 * noise2(nx, ny)

dna.label: PP-0002A
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Escher's 'Print Gallery' spiral: w = z^alpha in complex space. The transform maps a pattern into a self-similar spiral — zoom in and the pattern repeats. Log-polar coordinates rotate and scale simultaneously. Mined from Shadertoy conformal mapping and Reinder Nijhoff's Droste implementation.

body.expr: px = abs(x - 0.5); py = y - 0.5; rr = 0.5 * (height + bot_r + top_r) / bulge; da = rr - bot_r; db = rr - top_r; vy = (db * db - da * da - height * height) / (2.0 * height); vx = sqrt(max(da * da - vy * vy, 0.0)); k = py * vx - px * vy; dx1 = px + vx; dy1 = py + vy; d1 = sqrt(dx1 * dx1 + dy1 * dy1) - rr; d2a = sqrt(px * px + py * py) - bot_r; dy2 = py - height; d2b = sqrt(px * px + dy2 * dy2) - top_r; d2 = min(d2a, d2b); d = (k > 0.0 && k < height * (px + vx)) ? d1 : d2; smoothstep(blur, 0.0, d)

dna.label: PP-0002B
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Inigo Quilez 2D SDF — egg shape. Two circles (bottom radius bot_r, top radius top_r) offset vertically by height, connected by a smooth envelope controlled by bulge. An asymmetric oval with tunable proportions — the parent shape for any tapered organic form. Source: iquilezles.org/articles/distfunctions2d

body.expr: dx = x - 0.5; dy = y - 0.5; r = sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy); phase = (r - t * speed * 0.05) * freq; envelope = pow(2.71828, 0.0 - phase * phase * damping); osc = cos(phase * 6.28318); 0.5 + 0.5 * envelope * osc

dna.label: PP-0002C
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Damped oscillating shockwave: a radial wavefront that decays with a Gaussian envelope. The cosine oscillation inside the envelope creates the elastic bounce — rings of alternating bright/dark that fade with distance from the wavefront. Speed moves the wavefront outward over time. Mined from LYGIA animation/easing elastic functions applied spatially.

body.expr: py = y * freq; n = noise2(py, t * speed); d = abs(x - 0.5 - n * warp); glow = pow(clamp(1.0 - d / thick, 0.0, 1.0), falloff); clamp(glow, 0.0, 1.0)

dna.label: PP-0002D
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: A vertical centre-line displaced horizontally by 1D noise sampled along y. pow() falloff gives the glow halo. Speed drives the noise time axis — fast = flickering lightning, slow = drifting smoke trail.

body.expr: px = abs(x - 0.5); py = abs(y - 0.5); d = (sqrt(px * px / (ax * ax) + py * py / (ay * ay)) - 1.0) * min(ax, ay); smoothstep(blur, 0.0, d)

dna.label: PP-0002E
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Approximate 2D SDF for ellipse. Uses the level-set (length(p/ab)-1)*min(ab) approximation rather than the exact Newton-iteration solution. Visually accurate for moderate aspect ratios (up to ~2:1). The exact IQ ellipse requires acos and cube root with branching — deferred to a future version if precision matters. Source: iquilezles.org/articles/distfunctions2d (simplified)

body.expr: n1 = noise2(x * scale1 + t * drift, y * scale1); n2 = noise2(x * scale2 + 5.7 + t * drift * 0.7, y * scale2 + 3.1); diff = (n1 - n2) * contrast; clamp(0.5 + diff, 0.0, 1.0)

dna.label: PP-0002F
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Two noise layers subtracted, creating cliff/erosion boundaries. t06 erosion patterns.

body.expr: turbulence2(x * scale + t * drift, y * scale, octaves, 2.0, 0.5)

dna.label: PP-00030
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Fractal Brownian motion noise field. st_004 in taste_07 — the noise rig. Lacunarity 2, gain 0.5 (standard fbm). One abs() is the difference between a cloud and a fire.

body.expr: sy = y * strand_count; strand = floor(sy); frac = sy - strand; along = x; nx = noise2(strand * 1.7 + t * speed, along * 3.0); disp = nx * wildness * along * along; shifted = frac + disp; d = abs(shifted - 0.5); smoothstep(0.12, 0.0, d)

dna.label: PP-00031
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Parallel strands with noise displacement increasing along their length, like pulling apart a feather. t06_025 pen-walk feather.

body.expr: px = x * scale + t * drift; py = y * scale; n = turbulence2(px, py, octaves, 2.0, 0.5); flame = pow(abs(n * 2.0 - 1.0), sharpness); clamp(flame, 0.0, 1.0)

dna.label: PP-00032
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Abs-folded turbulence from st_004 in taste_07. 'One abs() is the difference between a cloud and a fire.' The fold creates ridges and creases. Sharpness dials between fire and cloud.

body.expr: dx = x - 0.5; dy = y - 0.5; r = sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy) + 0.0001; a = atan2(dy, dx) + t * speed; petal = abs(cos(a * petals * 0.5)); d = r - size * petal; smoothstep(blur, 0.0, 0.0 - d)

dna.label: PP-00033
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Flower rosette SDF: radius modulated by abs(cos(angle * N/2)). Creates organic petal shapes — the cosine lobes pull the radius outward at N evenly spaced angles. PolarRose uses sin(n*theta) for a polar curve; this uses abs(cos) for a filled petal shape. Mined from LYGIA sdf/flowerSDF.

body.expr: ca = cos(t * speed * 0.5); sa = sin(t * speed * 0.5); rx = (x - 0.5) * scale; ry = (y - 0.5) * scale; nx = rx * ca - ry * sa; ny = rx * sa + ry * ca; n1 = noise2(nx, ny); ca2 = cos(t * speed * 0.7 + 1.0); sa2 = sin(t * speed * 0.7 + 1.0); nx2 = rx * 2.0 * ca2 - ry * 2.0 * sa2 + 5.2; ny2 = rx * 2.0 * sa2 + ry * 2.0 * ca2 + 1.3; n2 = noise2(nx2, ny2); 0.5 + 0.5 * (n1 + n2 * 0.5) / 1.5

dna.label: PP-00034
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Flow noise: time-rotated coordinate sampling for smooth animation. Instead of sliding through a noise field (which creates visible drift), the sampling coordinates rotate over time — each octave at a different angular speed and phase. The result looks like slowly churning fluid. Two octaves at different frequencies and rotation rates create organic motion. Mined from Shadertoy flow noise implementations and Perlin's original flow noise paper.

body.expr: px = x * scale + t * drift; py = y * scale; w = sin(px) + sin(py * 0.7 + px * 0.3); f = abs(w * fold); f - floor(f)

dna.label: PP-00035
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Folded wave train from t06_051 taste — two sines combined then abs-folded via fract(abs(w*fold)). The fold count multiplies the creases. Low fold = gentle ripple; high fold = corrugated metal / topographic contour stacking.

body.expr: dx = x - 0.5; dy = y - 0.5; r = sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy) + 0.0001; a = atan2(dy, dx); seg = 6.28318 / max(folds, 1.0); a = a - seg * floor(a / seg + 0.5); a = abs(a); seg2 = seg / max(subfolds, 1.0); a = a - seg2 * floor(a / seg2 + 0.5); a = abs(a); nx = r * cos(a) * scale; ny = r * sin(a) * scale; 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(nx + t * speed) * cos(ny)

dna.label: PP-00036
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Nested rotational domain folds: the angle is folded into 1/N of the circle (primary folds), then folded again within that sector (subfolds). Two levels of angular abs-fold create nested kaleidoscopic symmetry — a fractal-like pattern from simple sin*cos in the folded domain. Distinct from MandalaFold (single-level fold) by the nested structure. Mined from Shadertoy fractal kaleidoscope shaders.

body.expr: dx = x - 0.5; dy = y - 0.5; r = sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy); a = atan2(dy, dx); golden = 2.39996; spiral = a - r * count * golden + t * speed * 6.28318; ring = 0.5 + 0.5 * cos(r * count * 6.28318); arm = 0.5 + 0.5 * cos(spiral * 5.0); dot = smoothstep(size + 0.01, size, r * abs(sin(spiral * count * 0.5))); clamp(ring * arm * 0.5 + dot * 0.5, 0.0, 1.0)

dna.label: PP-00037
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Fibonacci/golden angle spiral dot pattern. From t06_027 prime-structured arms.

body.expr: val = sqrt((x - 0.5) * (x - 0.5) + (y - 0.5) * (y - 0.5)) * scale; val = val - floor(val); lo = 0.5 * pow(max(2.0 * val, 0.0001), gain); hi = 1.0 - 0.5 * pow(max(2.0 - 2.0 * val, 0.0001), gain); (val < 0.5) ? lo : hi

dna.label: PP-00038
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Perlin's gain function applied spatially: redistributes a radial gradient's contrast. gain<1 flattens midtones (S-curve inverted), gain>1 pushes values toward 0 and 1 (S-curve). The formula 0.5*pow(2x,k) / 1-0.5*pow(2-2x,k) is symmetric and C1-continuous at x=0.5. Applied to a repeating radial distance field, it sculpts the brightness profile of concentric rings. Mined from LYGIA math/gain and Perlin's bias/gain paper.

body.expr: dx = x - 0.5; dy = y - 0.5; r2 = dx * dx + dy * dy; pow(2.71828, 0.0 - r2 / max(sigma * sigma * 2.0, 0.0001)) * brightness

dna.label: PP-00039
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: True Gaussian bell curve applied radially: exp(-r^2 / 2*sigma^2). Unlike smoothstep or polynomial falloffs, this is the exact normal distribution shape — maximum at center, exponential decay, no hard edge. Sigma controls spread, brightness controls peak amplitude. The most physically correct soft spotlight. Mined from LYGIA draw/ Gaussian functions.

body.expr: dx = x - 0.5; dy = y - 0.5; r = sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy); a = atan2(dy, dx) + t * speed; tooth = depth * clamp(sin(a * teeth) * sharp, -1.0, 1.0) * 0.5 + depth * 0.5; gear_r = radius + tooth; d_outer = r - gear_r; d_inner = hub - r; d = max(d_outer, d_inner); smoothstep(0.005, 0.0, d)

dna.label: PP-0003A
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Toothed gear SDF: polar distance modulated by clamped sine for tooth profiles. The sharp param controls tooth squareness — low values give rounded bumps, high values give flat-topped teeth. Hub param carves the center hole. Mined from LYGIA sdf/gearSDF and Shadertoy mechanical pattern studies.

body.expr: dx = x - 0.5; dy = y - 0.5; d = sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy); s = 1.0; total = 0.0; s = s * decay; r1 = smoothstep(s + 0.005, s - 0.005, d); total = max(total, r1 * s); s = s * decay; r2 = smoothstep(s + 0.005, s - 0.005, d); total = max(total, r2 * s); s = s * decay; r3 = smoothstep(s + 0.005, s - 0.005, d); total = max(total, r3 * s); s = s * decay; r4 = smoothstep(s + 0.005, s - 0.005, d); total = max(total, r4 * s); s = s * decay; r5 = smoothstep(s + 0.005, s - 0.005, d); total = max(total, r5 * s); s = s * decay; r6 = smoothstep(s + 0.005, s - 0.005, d); total = max(total, r6 * s); s = s * decay; r7 = smoothstep(s + 0.005, s - 0.005, d); total = max(total, r7 * s); s = s * decay; r8 = smoothstep(s + 0.005, s - 0.005, d); total = max(total, r8 * s); s = s * decay; r9 = smoothstep(s + 0.005, s - 0.005, d); total = max(total, r9 * s); s = s * decay; r10 = smoothstep(s + 0.005, s - 0.005, d); total = max(total, r10 * s); a = atan2(dy, dx); wave = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(a * count + t * drift * 6.28318); total * wave

dna.label: PP-0003B
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Nested circles with geometric size decay — each circle 0.93x the last. Tunnel/perspective illusion. From t06_046 geometric-decay tunnel.

body.expr: k = 6.28318 / max(wavelength, 0.01); px = (x * cos(direction) + y * sin(direction)) * scale; ph = px * k - t * speed * sqrt(9.8 * scale / max(k, 0.01)); h = sin(ph - steepness * sin(ph)); 0.5 + 0.5 * h

dna.label: PP-0003C
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Gerstner ocean wave: sin(x - A*sin(x)) creates peaked crests and flat troughs, unlike regular sine waves. Steepness parameter A controls cusp sharpness — at 0 it is a sine wave, approaching 1 the crests become knife-sharp. The dispersion relation sqrt(g/k) gives physically correct wave speed. Mined from LYGIA generative/gerstnerWave and ocean rendering literature.

dna.label: PP-0003D
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Perlin gradient noise: hash to random gradient vector per grid corner, dot product with displacement, smooth cubic interpolation. From Book of Shaders ch.11 — the algorithm that changed procedural graphics. Distinct from value noise (interpolates scalars, creating blocky artifacts): gradient noise interpolates vectors, giving smooth directional lobes without grid alignment.

body.expr: wx = noise2(x * noise_scale + t * speed, y * noise_scale) * warp_amount; wy = noise2(x * noise_scale + 5.5, y * noise_scale + 3.3 + t * speed) * warp_amount; gx = sin((x + wx) * grid_freq * 6.28318); gy = sin((y + wy) * grid_freq * 6.28318); v = max(abs(gx), abs(gy)); smoothstep(0.9, 1.0, v)

dna.label: PP-0003E
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Regular grid deformed by noise displacement. Warped grid patterns.

body.expr: px = x * scale; py = y * scale; pz = t * drift; g = sin(px) * cos(py) + sin(py) * cos(pz) + sin(pz) * cos(px); clamp(1.0 - abs(g) / thresh, 0.0, 1.0)

dna.label: PP-0003F
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: The gyroid: sin(x)cos(y)+sin(y)cos(z)+sin(z)cos(x)=0. A triply-periodic minimal surface sliced by the z=t*drift plane. Nature uses it in butterfly wings and bone marrow. Threshold controls the wall thickness of the labyrinth.

body.expr: gx = floor(x * grid_size); gy = floor(y * grid_size); cx = (gx + 0.5) / grid_size; cy = (gy + 0.5) / grid_size; dx = x - cx; dy = y - cy; dist = sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy) * grid_size; wave = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(cx * wave_freq * 6.28318 + cy * wave_freq * 3.14159 + t * wave_speed); dot_radius = wave * 0.5; smoothstep(dot_radius + 0.02, dot_radius - 0.02, dist)

dna.label: PP-00040
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Dots sized by a wave field — halftone print effect. From t06 halftone patterns.

body.expr: seed = x * 94723.18 + y * 68107.29 + t * grain_speed * 173.91; h = abs(sin(seed) * 43758.5453); h = h - floor(h); h * intensity

dna.label: PP-00041
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Incoherent static/film grain: a high-frequency hash with no spatial coherence — each pixel gets an independent random value. Unlike noise2 (spatially smooth), this mimics photographic film grain or analog TV static. The large coordinate multipliers ensure decorrelation across adjacent pixels. Grain_speed controls temporal flickering rate. Mined from LYGIA generative/random and film grain shader techniques.

body.expr: dx = (x - 0.5) * scale; dy = (0.4 - y) * scale; r2 = dx * dx + dy * dy; h = r2 - 1.0; d = h * h * h - dx * dx * dy * dy * dy; clamp(-d * edge, 0.0, 1.0)

dna.label: PP-00042
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Algebraic heart curve: (x^2+y^2-1)^3 - x^2*y^3 = 0. The implicit equation that every Valentine card is built on whether it knows it or not. Scale controls size, edge controls boundary sharpness. Centered slightly above middle for visual balance (more bulk in the two bumps than the single point).

body.expr: px = abs(x - 0.5); py = abs(y - 0.5); dot = min(-0.866025 * px + 0.5 * py, 0.0); px = px + 1.732050 * dot; py = py - dot; px = px - clamp(px, -0.57735 * radius, 0.57735 * radius); py = py - radius; d = sqrt(px * px + py * py) * (py > 0.0 ? 1.0 : -1.0); smoothstep(blur, 0.0, d)

dna.label: PP-00043
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Inigo Quilez 2D SDF — regular hexagon via reflection folding. One reflection reduces the full hexagon to a single sector, then distance to the edge. The hex is the tile that bees discovered and GPUs keep rediscovering. Source: iquilezles.org/articles/distfunctions2d

body.expr: px = abs(x - 0.5); py = abs(y - 0.5); d1 = min(-0.5 * px + 0.866025 * py, 0.0); px = px + d1; py = py - 1.732051 * d1; d2 = min(0.866025 * px - 0.5 * py, 0.0); px = px - 1.732051 * d2; py = py + d2; px = px - clamp(px, radius * 0.577350, radius * 1.732051); py = py - radius; d = sqrt(px * px + py * py) * (py > 0.0 ? 1.0 : -1.0); smoothstep(blur, 0.0, d)

dna.label: PP-00044
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Inigo Quilez 2D SDF — hexagram (Star of David). Two reflections with hex symmetry constants. The six-pointed star formed by overlapping two equilateral triangles. Source: iquilezles.org/articles/distfunctions2d

body.expr: sx = x * scale; sy = y * scale * 1.1547; row = floor(sy); off = (row % 2) * 0.5; col = floor(sx + off); cx = col - off + 0.5; cy = (row + 0.5) / 1.1547; dx1 = abs(x * scale - cx); dy1 = abs(y * scale * 1.1547 - (row + 0.5)); cx2 = col + 1.0 - off + 0.5; dx2 = abs(x * scale - cx2); d1 = max(dx1, dy1 * 0.5 + dx1 * 0.5); d2 = max(dx2, dy1 * 0.5 + dx2 * 0.5); d = min(d1, d2); edge = abs(d - 0.5); smoothstep(thickness, 0.0, edge)

dna.label: PP-00045
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Hexagonal tiling pattern. Geometric tiling.

body.expr: sx = x * cells; sy = y * cells * 1.1547; row = floor(sy); parity = row - floor(row * 0.5) * 2.0; col = floor(sx - parity * 0.5); fx = sx - col - parity * 0.5 - 0.5; fy = sy - row - 0.5; h = abs(sin(col * 127.1 + row * 311.7) * 43758.5453); h = h - floor(h); a = floor(h * 6.0) * 1.0472; rx = fx * cos(a) - fy * sin(a); ry = fx * sin(a) + fy * cos(a); d1 = abs(sqrt((rx + 0.5) * (rx + 0.5) + ry * ry) - 0.3); d2 = abs(sqrt((rx - 0.25) * (rx - 0.25) + (ry - 0.433) * (ry - 0.433)) - 0.3); d3 = abs(sqrt((rx - 0.25) * (rx - 0.25) + (ry + 0.433) * (ry + 0.433)) - 0.3); d = min(d1, min(d2, d3)); smoothstep(width, 0.0, d)

dna.label: PP-00046
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Truchet tiling on a hexagonal grid: each hex cell gets one of 6 random orientations (60-degree increments), arcs drawn at the three alternating hex corners. The hex offset-row grid uses parity = row mod 2 to stagger columns. Creates flowing maze-like paths with hexagonal symmetry, distinct from square TruchetTile. Mined from Shadertoy hex Truchet variations.

body.expr: px = abs(x - 0.5); py = y - 0.5; cx = sin(opening); cy = cos(opening); l = sqrt(px * px + py * py); rx = -cx * px + cy * py; ry = cy * px + cx * py; fx = max(ry, rx) > 0.0 ? rx : l * (-cx > 0.0 ? 1.0 : -1.0); fy = rx > 0.0 ? ry : l; gx = fx - leg_w; gy = abs(fy - radius) - leg_len; mx = max(gx, 0.0); my = max(gy, 0.0); d = sqrt(mx * mx + my * my) + min(0.0, max(gx, gy)); smoothstep(blur, 0.0, d)

dna.label: PP-00047
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Inigo Quilez 2D SDF — horseshoe shape. A thick arc with straight legs extending from each end. dna.why: Three-state Truchet tiling: each cell randomly picks one of three configurations — arc pair A (corners 0,1 and 1,0), arc pair B (corners 0,0 and 1,1), or a centred circle. The third state breaks the binary monotony of standard Truchet, creating dead-ends and islands in the path network. Mined from Shadertoy multi-state Truchet explorations.

body.expr: gx = floor(x * cells); gy = floor(y * cells); fx = x * cells - gx; fy = y * cells - gy; h = abs(sin(gx * 127.1 + gy * 311.7) * 43758.5453); h = h - floor(h); da1 = abs(sqrt(fx * fx + (fy - 1.0) * (fy - 1.0)) - 0.5); da2 = abs(sqrt((fx - 1.0) * (fx - 1.0) + fy * fy) - 0.5); da = min(da1, da2); db1 = abs(sqrt(fx * fx + fy * fy) - 0.5); db2 = abs(sqrt((fx - 1.0) * (fx - 1.0) + (fy - 1.0) * (fy - 1.0)) - 0.5); db = min(db1, db2); fa = smoothstep(width, 0.0, da); fb = smoothstep(width, 0.0, db); s = (h > 0.5) ? 1.0 : 0.0; over = fa * (1.0 - s) + fb * s; under = fb * (1.0 - s) + fa * s; over + under * (1.0 - over) * 0.4

dna.label: PP-00094
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Intertwined Truchet arcs: both arc pairs drawn per cell with over-under occlusion. The hash determines which pair is 'over' (full brightness) vs 'under' (40% brightness, occluded by the over). Creates a woven fabric illusion from the same math as TruchetTile. Mined from Smith (1987) and Shadertoy Truchet variations.

body.expr: px = abs(x - 0.5); py = -(y - 0.5); qx = px - tunnel_w; qy = py - tunnel_h; mx1 = max(qx, 0.0); d1 = mx1 * mx1 + qy * qy; lp = sqrt(px * px + py * py); qx2 = py > 0.0 ? qx : lp - tunnel_w; my2 = max(qy, 0.0); d2 = qx2 * qx2 + my2 * my2; dd = sqrt(min(d1, d2)); d = max(qx2, qy) < 0.0 ? -dd : dd; smoothstep(blur, 0.0, d)

dna.label: PP-00095
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Inigo Quilez 2D SDF — tunnel (arch shape). A rectangle with a semicircular top — the tunnel mouth, the cathedral window, the archway. The semicircle smoothly joins the straight walls. Source: iquilezles.org/articles/distfunctions2d

body.expr: dx = x - 0.5; dy = y - 0.5; a = atan2(dy, dx); r = sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy) + 0.0001; angular = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(a * rays); radial = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(depth / r - t * speed); angular * radial

dna.label: PP-00096
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Radial lines from centre with sin modulation creating a tunnel fly-through. t06_046 warp tunnel.

body.expr: px = x * scale + t * drift; py = y * scale; n = turbulence2(px, py, octaves, 2.0, 0.5); abs(n * 2.0 - 1.0)

dna.label: PP-00097
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: abs(noise) gives turbulence/fire look. One abs() is the difference between a cloud and a fire. From st_004 turbulence fold in taste_07.

body.expr: cx = floor(x * cols); cy = floor(y * rows); fx = x * cols - cx; fy = y * rows - cy; dc = sqrt((cx / cols - 0.5) * (cx / cols - 0.5) + (cy / rows - 0.5) * (cy / rows - 0.5)); angle = dc * twist + t * speed; ca = cos(angle); sa = sin(angle); rx = (fx - 0.5) * ca - (fy - 0.5) * sa; ry = (fx - 0.5) * sa + (fy - 0.5) * ca; smoothstep(size + 0.01, size, max(abs(rx), abs(ry)))

dna.label: PP-00098
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Per-tile rotation proportional to distance from grid centre. Squares become diamonds become a spiral vortex. The 2D rotation matrix applied to tile-local coordinates — what Book of Shaders calls 'rotating the coordinate system, not the shape.' Twist controls radial rotation rate, speed animates the whole field.

body.expr: px = abs(x - 0.5); py = y - 0.5; bb = (bot_r - top_r) / height; aa = sqrt(max(1.0 - bb * bb, 0.0)); k = px * (-bb) + py * aa; d1 = sqrt(px * px + py * py) - bot_r; dy2 = py - height; d2 = sqrt(px * px + dy2 * dy2) - top_r; d3 = px * aa + py * bb - bot_r; d = k < 0.0 ? d1 : (k > aa * height ? d2 : d3); smoothstep(blur, 0.0, d)

dna.label: PP-00099
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Inigo Quilez 2D SDF — uneven capsule. Two semicircles of different radii (bot_r, top_r) connected by tangent lines, separated vertically by height. A tapered pill shape — the bone, the limb, the connector between thick and thin. Source: iquilezles.org/articles/distfunctions2d

body.expr: px = x * scale; py = y * scale; eps = 0.01; n0 = turbulence2(px, py, 4, 2.0, 0.5); nx = turbulence2(px + eps, py, 4, 2.0, 0.5); ny = turbulence2(px, py + eps, 4, 2.0, 0.5); gx2 = (nx - n0) / eps; gy2 = (ny - n0) / eps; grad = sqrt(gx2 * gx2 + gy2 * gy2); clamp(grad * gain, 0.0, 1.0)

dna.label: PP-0009A
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Gradient magnitude of turbulence — the finite-difference derivative finds where the noise field changes fastest. Those are the edges, ridges, veins. Three noise lookups per pixel (center, +dx, +dy) to approximate the partial derivatives.

body.expr: px = x - 0.5; py = y - 0.5; d1 = sqrt((px + sep) * (px + sep) + py * py) - radius; d2 = sqrt((px - sep) * (px - sep) + py * py) - radius; d = max(d1, d2); smoothstep(blur, 0.0, d)

dna.label: PP-0009B
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Vesica piscis — the lens formed by intersecting two circles. SDF intersection via max(d1,d2). Sep controls the gap between circle centres: sep=0 collapses to a full circle, sep approaching radius thins to a sliver. The sacred geometry shape that keeps showing up in Gothic windows and Venn diagrams. Source: iquilezles.org/articles/distfunctions2d

body.expr: f1 = voronoi2(x * scale + t * drift, y * scale, 1, jitter); f2 = voronoi2(x * scale + t * drift, y * scale, 2, jitter); ratio = f1 / max(f2, 0.001); glow = pow(1.0 - clamp(ratio, 0.0, 1.0), sharpness); glow

dna.label: PP-0009C
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Voronoi edge glow from F1/F2 ratio. At cell centers F1/F2 approaches 0 (dark), at edges it approaches 1 (bright). The pow(1-ratio, sharpness) inversion makes edges glow. CrackedMud uses F2-F1 for hard crack lines; this uses the ratio for soft luminous edges. Mined from Shadertoy voronoi techniques.

body.expr: d = voronoi2(x * scale, y * scale, 0, jitter); clamp(0.5 + 0.5 * sin(d * rings + t * speed), 0.0, 1.0)

dna.label: PP-0009D
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Voronoi distance field wrapped through sin() — from t06_244 crystallized taste. Each cell gets concentric rings like a topographic map of a crystal lattice. The sharp creases at Voronoi seams are free — they come from the distance function discontinuity.

body.expr: px = x * scale; py = y * scale; qx = turbulence2(px + t * speed, py, 3, 2.0, 0.5); qy = turbulence2(px + 5.2, py + 1.3, 3, 2.0, 0.5); turbulence2(px + warp * qx, py + warp * qy, octaves, 2.0, 0.5)

dna.label: PP-0009E
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Warped fBm: turbulence warps turbulence — f(p) = fbm(p + fbm(p)). From Book of Shaders ch.13. DomainWarp uses noise2 (single-octave, smooth) for warping; WarpedFBM uses turbulence2 (multi-octave, detailed) for richer, more organic cloud-like structures with deeper self-similarity.

body.expr: wx = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(x * freq_x * 6.28318 + t * speed); wy = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(y * freq_y * 6.28318 + t * speed * 0.7); wx * wy

dna.label: PP-0009F
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Two crossing wave patterns creating a mesh/fabric. From t06 fabric patterns.

body.expr: px = x * cols; py = y * rows; dx = px + sin(py * waveFreq + t * speed) * waveAmp; dy = py + sin(px * waveFreq + t * speed) * waveAmp; gx = abs(dx - floor(dx + 0.5)); gy = abs(dy - floor(dy + 0.5)); d = min(gx, gy); smoothstep(width, 0.0, d)

dna.label: PP-000A0
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Sine-distorted grid: regular grid lines wobble with sinusoidal displacement. GridWarp uses noise for organic warping; WavyGrid uses pure sine for rhythmic, breath-like motion. Useful for textile, water surface, and op-art patterns.

body.expr: gx = floor(x * cells); gy = floor(y * cells); fx = x * cells - gx - 0.5; fy = y * cells - gy - 0.5; bx = gx - floor(gx * 0.5) * 2.0; by = gy - floor(gy * 0.5) * 2.0; rot = (bx + by * 2.0) * 1.5708; rx = fx * cos(rot) - fy * sin(rot); ry = fx * sin(rot) + fy * cos(rot); 0.5 + 0.5 * sin((rx + ry) * detail * 6.28318 + t * speed)

dna.label: PP-000A1
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Pinwheel-rotated square tiles: each 2x2 block of cells has tiles rotated 0, 90, 180, 270 degrees based on position parity. A diagonal stripe pattern inside each tile appears to spin like windmill blades. The rotation uses position-in-block (bx + by*2) mapped to quarter-turn multiples. Mined from LYGIA space/ tile rotation and Islamic geometric pattern literature.

body.expr: dx = x - 0.5; dy = y - 0.5; d = sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy); n = noise2(x * scale + t * drift, y * scale); v = sin(d * freq + n * warp); 0.5 + 0.5 * v

dna.label: PP-000A2
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Wood grain: sin(radial_distance + noise * warp) creates concentric growth rings distorted by noise. From Book of Shaders ch.13 — the companion to MarbleVein. Freq controls ring density, warp controls organic distortion.

body.expr: sx = sin(y * grid_freq * 6.28318 + t * speed) * wave_amount; sy = sin(x * grid_freq * 6.28318 + t * speed * 0.8) * wave_amount; warp_x = x + sx; warp_y = y + sy; gx = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(warp_x * grid_freq * 6.28318); gy = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(warp_y * grid_freq * 6.28318); cell = floor(x * grid_freq) + floor(y * grid_freq); over = (cell % 2 == 0) ? gx * (1.0 - gy * 0.5) : gy * (1.0 - gx * 0.5); clamp(over, 0.0, 1.0)

dna.label: PP-000A3
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Two perpendicular wave patterns with over-under weave illusion. From t06 weave/fabric patterns.

dna.author: makers-factory

body.expr: px = x * cols; tri = abs(px - floor(px + 0.5)) * 2.0; sy = y * rows + tri * amplitude; d = abs(sy - floor(sy + 0.5)); smoothstep(width, 0.0, d)

dna.label: PP-000A5
dna.author: makers-factory
dna.why: Chevron/zigzag stripes: triangle wave offsets horizontal stripes to create V-shaped patterns. Amplitude controls the zigzag depth, rows controls stripe density. The simplest geometric pattern that creates directional visual flow without curves.
